A297469.name: Solution (bb(n)) of the system of 3 complementary equations in Comments.
comment: Define sequences aa(n), bb(n), cc(n) recursively, starting with aa(0) = 1, bb(0) = 2, cc(0) = 3:
where "least new k" means the least positive integer not yet placed.
The sequences aa,bb,cc partition the positive integers. It appears that cc = A047218 and that for every n >= 0,
(3) 5*n - 3 - bb(n) is in {0,1} for every n >= 0;
Conjecture: For t >= 0, bb(2t) = 10t + 1 (+1 if binary expansion of t ends in an odd number of 0's), bb(2t+1) = 10t + 7.
The first part may also be written as bb(2t) = 10t + 1 + A328789(t-1).
link: Clark Kimberling, Table of n, a(n) for n = 0..10000 [This is the sequence bb]

A297464.name: Solution (a(n)) of the system of 4 complementary equations in Comments.
comment: Define sequences a(n), b(n), c(n), d(n) recursively, starting with a(0) = 1, b(0) = 2, c(0) = 3;:
where "least new k" means the least positive integer not yet placed.

The sequences a,b,c,d partition the positive integers.  The sequence d can be called the "anti-tribonacci sequence"; viz., if sequences a and b are defined as above, and c(n) is defined by c(n) = a(n) + b(n), then the resulting system of 3 complementary sequences gives c = A075326, the "anti-Fibonacci sequence."  See A299409 for the "anti-tetranacci" sequences.
link: Clark Kimberling, Table of n, a(n) for n = 0..1000
Wieb Bosma, Rene Bruin, Robbert Fokkink, Jonathan Grube, Anniek Reuijl, and Thian Tromp, Using Walnut to solve problems from the OEIS, arXiv:2503.04122 [math.NT], 2025. See p. 8.
mathematica: a = {1}; b = {2}; c = {3}; d = {}; AppendTo[d, Last[a] + Last[b] + Last[c]];

A328789.name: Expansion of (chi(x^3) / chi(-x^2))^2 in powers of x where chi() is a Ramanujan theta function.
comment: Ramanujan theta functions: f(q) (see A121373), phi(q) (A000122), psi(q) (A010054), chi(q) (A000700).
G.f. is a period 1 Fourier series which satisfies f(-1 / (36 t)) = 1/2 g(t) where q = exp(2 Pi i t) and g() is g.f. for A328795.
link: Eric Weisstein's World of Mathematics, Ramanujan Theta Functions
formula: Expansion of q^(1/12) * (eta(q^4) * eta(q^6)^2)^2 / (eta(q^2) * eta(q^3) * eta(q^12))^2 in powers of q.
mathematica: a[ n_] := SeriesCoefficient[ (QPochhammer[ -x^2, x^2] QPochhammer[ -x^3, x^6])^2, {x, 0, n}];
program: (PARI) {a(n) = my(A); if( n < 0, 0, A = x * O(x^n); polcoeff( (eta(x^4 + A) * eta(x^6 + A)^2)^2 / (eta(x^2 + A) * eta(x^3 + A) * eta(x^12 + A))^2, n))};
A328789.author: _Michael Somos_, Oct 27 2019

A047218.name: Numbers that are congruent to {0, 3} mod 5.
comment: Multiples of 5 interleaved with 2 less than multiples of 5. - _Wesley Ivan Hurt_, Oct 19 2013
Numbers k such that k^2/5 + k*(k + 1)/10 = k*(3*k + 1)/10 is a nonnegative integer. - _Bruno Berselli_, Feb 14 2017
For n >= 2, also the vertex cover number of the (n-1)-necklace graph. - _Eric W. Weisstein_, Feb 17 2026
For n >= 4, also the diameter of the n-cube connected cycle graph.  - _Eric W. Weisstein_, Feb 25 2026

Index entries for linear recurrences with constant coefficients, signature (1,1,-1).
formula: a(n) = 5*n - a(n-1) - 7 for n>1, a(1)=0. - _Vincenzo Librandi_, Aug 05 2010
a(n+1) = Sum_{k>=0} A030308(n,k)*b(k) with b(0)=3 and b(k)=A020714(k-1)=5*2^(k-1) for k>0. - _Philippe Deléham_, Oct 17 2011
a(n) = floor(5*n/2)-2 = 3*n - 3 - floor((n-1)/2). - _Wesley Ivan Hurt_, Oct 14 2013
a(n+1) = n + (n + (n + (n mod 2))/2). - _Wesley Ivan Hurt_, Oct 19 2013
Sum_{n>=2} (-1)^n/a(n) = log(5)/4 - sqrt(5)*log(phi)/10 - sqrt(1-2/sqrt(5))*Pi/10, where phi is the golden ratio (A001622). - _Amiram Eldar_, Dec 07 2021

With[{c5 = 5 Range[0, 30]}, Riffle[c5, c5 + 3]] (* _Harvey P. Dale_, Apr 02 2017 *)
